### Summary

The redo machinery itself (how $\Delta t$[^rg-e08a4caa8890] is halved, what the driver does with the return value) belongs to
@sec-ch07-redo and is outlined in @sec-ch01-driver. This section covers the two causes moist physics raises and the
parts of the rule that matter to them. A species deficit that the conserved limiter repairs
(@sec-ch10-borrow, @sec-ch10-fixvapor) sets the limiter mark, cause 4, when it was larger than round-off of the
cell's gas density before the repair; how far the repair then moved other cells does not count. A cell that the saturation adjustment
(@sec-ch10-satadj) failed to bring to equilibrium is counted by kintera, and a non-zero count after the step is
cause 16. Either one, on any rank, rejects the step everywhere.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Rejects a step for a species deficit above round-off (cause 4) or a failed saturation cell (cause 16).

**Data.** Reads the block's limiter marks and kintera's failure count; writes their two bits of the cause word.

**Placement.** Counter drained at stage 0 and once more after the step, in `check_redo`; rule in @sec-ch07-redo.

**Activation.** Cause 4 with `limiter: true`; cause 16 with a ThermoY; `max_redo` (default 5) is set from code only.

**Guarantee / limits.** Either cause on any rank rejects the step everywhere; past `max_redo` the run ends unrestored.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch10-redo-tests; `test_check_redo_saturation_python`, `test_forcing.release`, `redo_check.py` `[C1]`–`[C3]`.
:::

Local symbols: $f_\iota$, $\iota=0..5$, the six redo flags of a rank, each 0 or 1, and
$c_{\mathrm{redo}}=\sum_\iota2^\iota f_\iota$ the cause word ($\iota$ is the bit index: $r$[^rg-0cf14ab9beae], $i$[^rg-9ac74714d98c], $j$, $k$[^rg-362f2334766b] are reserved).

The saturation cause is always on when the thermo has a ThermoY; the limiter cause is on with `limiter: true`.
What a redo restores, and how the step is retried, is @sec-ch07-redo.

### Derivation

The scheme is a decision rule, not a discretization. Its why-steps are:

1. *Six flags, one bit each.* `local_redo_flag_tensor` forms six 0/1 flags $f_\iota$ (and a seventh entry, the step's
   CUDA vapour-repair failures, which `read_redo_flags` raises as an error and does not pack; @sec-ch10-fixvapor);
   `reduce_redo_flags` packs the six as
   $c_{\mathrm{redo}}=\sum_\iota2^\iota f_\iota$, so the limiter repair is bit 4 ($\iota=2$) and the saturation failure bit 16 ($\iota=4$) (`[C1]`).
2. *One rank's failure is every rank's.* The flags are reduced with MAX over ranks before packing. For 0/1 values
   MAX is OR, so the packed word is the bitwise OR of every rank's word, and every rank takes the same decision
   (`[C2]`, all 4096 two-rank combinations).
3. *A redo restores and retries with a smaller step* (@sec-ch07-redo). `apply_redo` restores the saved state unless the attempt count exceeds
   `max_redo`; past it, a step with a moist cause terminates with the rejected state in memory, and only the
   VIC[^rg-132a64cd545b] cause 32 restores first (`[C3]`).
4. *No round-off enters the decision.* The flags are integers compared and OR-ed exactly; the only rounded quantity
   is the species density before the limiter's repair, which must be below $-4096\,\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ times the
   cell's total gas density to set bit 4 ($\iota=2$). The bound is `species_repair_mark`, `kSpeciesRepairMarkUlp`
   ulp, defined equal to `kPositivityRoundoffUlp` (64 float32 ulp in float32)
   ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}},
   {{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.hpp kSpeciesRepairMarkUlp >}}; @sec-ch10-fixvapor).

::: {.callout-important title="Check"}
A line-for-line port of the rule checks steps 1 to 3:[^redo-c] bits 4 and 16 (`[C1]`); MAX is OR over two ranks
(`[C2]`); termination without restore past `max_redo` (`[C3]`).
:::

[^redo-c]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch10/checks/redo_check.py`, output `redo_check.out`, lines `[C1]`–`[C3]`; a numpy
    port of `MeshBlockImpl::reduce_redo_flags` and `MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo` at the pin, double precision.
    Run on CPU, one process, with Python 3.12.10, sympy 1.14.0 and numpy 2.5.3; the output matches the committed file.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch10-redo-flow shows the decision. The saturation counter is drained once at the start of every step, so a
failure counted by a ThermoY call between steps (a diagnostic from Python, say) is not charged to the next step,
`saturation_failures` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}). After the step,
`local_redo_flag_tensor` reads the limiter marks after the floor test's conversion, so a repair that conversion
makes counts as cause 4, and drains the saturation counter exactly once for cause 16
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flag_tensor >}}). How the flags are read back and reduced
over blocks and ranks is @sec-ch07-redo.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch10-redo-flow
#| fig-cap: "Step acceptance for the moist causes. Each box is one step of the decision, read top to bottom; the last three boxes are the three outcomes. Green outlines mark operations, black arrows the order."
#| fig-alt: "Five boxes in a column: local flags; MAX over blocks and ranks; accept; restore and redo; terminate."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch10.figures.fig_redo_flow import make_fig
make_fig()
```

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| entry point | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::check_redo >}} | `check_redo` | |
| the six flags | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flag_tensor >}} | `local_redo_flag_tensor` | |
| restore or accept | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}} | `apply_redo` | `max_redo` |
| saturation counter | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::saturation_failures >}} | `saturation_failures` | |
| kintera's counter | [`kintera thermo_y.cpp:385-390`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp#L385-L390) | `take_saturation_adjustment_failures` | |
| default of `max_redo` | [`pyharp integrator.hpp:58`](https://github.com/chengcli/pyharp/blob/4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29/src/integrator/integrator.hpp#L58) | `max_redo` | `max_redo` |

: Code map of the moist redo causes. {#tbl-ch10-redo-code}

1. Drain the counter at stage 0, `saturation_failures` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}).
2. Form the six local flags and the vapour-repair entry on the device, `local_redo_flag_tensor`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flag_tensor >}}), and read them back in one copy,
   raising on the vapour entry, `read_redo_flags` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::read_redo_flags >}}).
3. Reduce with MAX over ranks and pack the bits, `reduce_redo_flags`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reduce_redo_flags >}}).
4. Name the causes in the log line, `causes` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}}).
5. Terminate past `max_redo` unless cause 32, `max_redo` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}}).
6. Restore the saved state, recompute the primitives and the scalar ratios, `drop_gravity_work_fix`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}}).

The user-visible messages are the log line "Redoing the step with smaller dt (causes: ...)" and "Maximum number of
redo attempts exceeded. Terminating.", both in `apply_redo`.

**How to use it.** The two causes need no key of their own: cause 4 comes with `limiter: true`, cause 16 with
a reactions list in the card. The retry limit is the integrator's `max_redo`, default 5, which the YAML card cannot
set: `integration`[^rg-0be2640247d0] accepts only `implicit-scheme`[^rg-2e5bfa0a6fb1], `implicit-advection-cfl`[^rg-8921bb46e24b], `shear-cfl`[^rg-a8ca523c043d] and pyharp's `type`, `cfl`[^rg-aface2df2155],
`tlim`[^rg-63bbb573ebd8], `nlim`[^rg-329666f99cd7], `ncycle_out`[^rg-c969ece96591], `verbose`, so a `max_redo` key is refused with "unknown key 'integration/max_redo'"
({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=1 >}}). A Python driver sets it on the
options before building the block:

```python
from snapy import MeshBlock, MeshBlockOptions
op = MeshBlockOptions.from_yaml("deck.yaml")
op.intg().max_redo(2)        # default 5
block = MeshBlock(op)
```

The decision of steps 2 and 3 is these lines ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}}):

```cpp
    if (pintg->current_redo > pintg->options->max_redo() && !(causes & 32)) {
```

`causes` is the packed word $c_{\mathrm{redo}}$ of step 1; the comparison is the termination of step 3, skipped for the VIC cause.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_check_redo_saturation_python` | five arms, saturation cause alone | logical | failure protocol |
| `test_check_redo_parallel.release` | one decision on 2 ranks | exact | saved tensors copied back |
| `test_forcing.release` | a species deficit redoes; a round-off deficit does not | ulp bound | `kSpeciesRepairMarkUlp` |
| `test_uranus_cycle1_abort.release` | column survives; abort exits nonzero | exit status | log strings |

: Tests of the moist redo causes; all pass at the pin.[^redo-ctest] {#tbl-ch10-redo-tests}

`test_check_redo_saturation` starts from one $\mathrm{NH_4SH}$ cell 150 times supersaturated. With `max-iter: 1` at
least one cell is left unadjusted, and the step must be redone with the saturation cause alone and then accepted; a
control step with the default `max-iter` must be clean; a failure counted between steps must not be charged; and a
two-block `Mesh` with the cell in block 1 must read block 1's count
({{< code tests/test_check_redo_saturation.py >}}). The `test_forcing` cases put $-10^{-4}$ in a species at stage 1
and require cause 4. A deficit of $-10^{-300}$ in a cloud-free cell is repaired but not redone, and so is a
$-10^{-300}$ vapour next to a cell of $0.01$ vapour, because the mark reads the deficit and not what the column
repair moved; $-10^{-9}$, above the bound, is redone
({{< code tests/test_forcing.cpp forcing.limiter_species_repair_redoes_the_step >}},
{{< code tests/test_forcing.cpp forcing.limiter_roundoff_species_repair_is_not_redone >}}). The CUDA arm
`test_check_redo_saturation_cuda_python` exists only in CUDA builds; the 2-rank test is the only multi-rank evidence.
Every ctest named here that the CPU build registers passed at the pin; the CUDA arm is not registered in that build
and was not run.[^redo-ctest]

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
A failure that a smaller time step cannot cure exhausts `max_redo` and ends the run. A species deficit above
round-off redoes the step even when it would be harmless; a smaller one is repaired without a redo.
:::

- A driver that carries state across a rejected step which the restore does not reset can make every attempt
  fail; what the restore covers is listed in @sec-ch07-redo.
- Past `max_redo` a moist failure terminates with the rejected state in memory; only the VIC cause restores first
  (`redo_check.py` `[C3]`).
- Moist redo combinations are absent from the switch coverage matrix (@sec-ch12-matrix).
